_about: Registry of the Atlas tools: one entry per tool, with its section, its route, the old addresses that redirect to it, the tools it requires and its release gates. The public flag decides whether a production build carries the tool's pages and links; preview deployments and local builds carry every Atlas tool. A tool goes public only after Swann records Lorenzo Pupillo's no-objection in the pull request; then empty its gates list, set public to true, set publishedAt, and make its legacy redirects permanent in vercel.json. Tools of site ai are never built on the Atlas; tools of site research are built only on Swann's machine; tools of site elsewhere are kept for another website: built only on Swann's machine, at a route under /elsewhere, and never linked or named from an Atlas page (Swann, 2 October 2026). The migration approach is kept the same way, off the Atlas, until Swann decides its return (5 October 2026); vercel.json sends its old address, /prepare/approach, to /prepare. The Standards Cascade's gate also covers the Standards overview (/standards), built wherever the Cascade is (5 October 2026), and the page of each standard, built only on Swann's machine. On 8 October 2026 Swann confirmed in writing that Lorenzo Pupillo has no objection, and the six Atlas tools (readiness, exposure, cascade, dates, inventory, suppliers) went public on www.qscatlas.app; the release notes follow on their own dates.
